images.filename: Composite map of Festiniog Railway Ordnance Survey 1 25000.jpg
images.caption: OS map showing the Ffestiniog Railway about 1953, at a scale of 1:25,000. The map shows the railway after the construction of the Llyn Ystradau reservoir flooded a section of the track bed, but before the deviation was built to carry the railway around the western shore of the reservoir. The map is a composite of sheets SH 63, SH 64, SH 74 (1953) and SH 53 (1956)
images.alt: OS map showing the Ffestiniog Railway about 1953, at a scale of 1:25,000. The map shows the railway after the construction of the Llyn Ystradau reservoir flooded a section of the track bed, but before the deviation was built to carry the railway around the western shore of the reservoir. The map is a composite of sheets SH 63, SH 64, SH 74 (1953) and SH 53 (1956)

images.caption:
Blaenau Ffestiniog railway station - On the left of the picture, Arriva Trains Wales British Rail Class 153 DMU 153327 stands at the standard gauge platform for a Conwy Valley Line service. While on the right of the picture the narrow gauge Ffestiniog Railway locomotive Linda is about to run-round the train in preparation for the journey to Porthmadog.

Note also the different platform heights for the different gauges.

images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
